result:
Good: automatic clean-up it is. I'll record that as your pick.

This is a project, not a small change. It has a volunteer upload page, the clean-up step, the visitor player with its remembered language, and the codes beside each exhibit. The design will be a proper written document, kept with the museum's website files. A reviewer will read it before you do, and I may come back once with a few questions from that.

Before I write it, there are two things the design still needs. I'll take them one at a time.

The first is something I haven't asked yet: **what's prompting the audio guide now, and what would tell you a year from now that it's working?** Your answer decides what the guide is built around. That covers what a visitor sees when they scan, what volunteers are asked to do, and what counts as done.

The second comes after that. The website today is a set of fixed pages with no way to accept uploads. Letting volunteers add recordings without asking anyone technical can be done a few different ways, with real trade-offs in cost and upkeep. I'll set those out with my recommendation before I write anything up.
